Subject: Realtime stream stalls during demo session

Hi Mateo —

We ran the extended demo this morning against the trial instance and hit repeated stalls during the live transcript: the client reported silent periods of ~6–12s where tokens stopped arriving, then a 101 reconnect or socket reset. The UI shows the connection as open but no payload arrives until a reconnect. This is happening across two separate regions we spun up.

I attached a short pcap and some server-side logs (ops collected). The behavior started about 09:04 PT and recurred ~every 7–12 minutes. This kills our ability to demo the low-latency experience and is a blocker for our pilot.

Can you confirm priority and next steps? We’re happy to do a joint troubleshooting call.

Thanks,
Sara Li

Quick initial read of the attachments:
- The pcap shows a clean TCP connection with continuous keepalives; however, token payload frames stop for ~6–10s prior to a TCP FIN in one instance. No obvious retransmit storms.
- Server logs show a repeated pattern where the model worker hits a transient 503 from the accelerator driver at high concurrent seq lengths, then falls back to a compatible quantized variant. That fallback delayed subsequent token emission until KV cache warmed back up. We see this at roughly minute intervals under sustained interactive load.

Hypothesis: a resource/retry path inside the worker leads to a stall window (not a pure proxy/socket drop). The 101 reconnects look like client-side fallback after heartbeat timeouts when chunks stop.

Immediate mitigations I can apply:
1) Turn on conservative batching limits for Nebula traffic (cap concurrent requests per worker).
2) Temporarily pin Nebula to the lower-latency model variant that we verified under load (avoids the driver fallback).
3) Enable per-connection debug frames so we can capture exact token timestamps going forward.

I’ll push those changes to the trial cluster now and will follow up in 30–45m with results. If we still see pauses I recommend an exec-level conference with Nebula to discuss an SLA carve-out while we tune.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Realtime stream stalls during demo session — update and next steps

Sara / Gabe — follow-up after the mitigations. Summary:
- We applied conservative batching and pinned Nebula trial to the verified low-latency variant on 22 Mar at 10:20 PT. Over 36 hours of simulated and customer-driven traffic we did not observe the 6–12s silent windows that you reported.
- The root cause appears to be an accelerator driver transient that triggers a synchronous fallback path inside the worker; that path stalls token emission while the KV cache is reinitialized. The fallbacks occurred under sustained high-concurrency sequences (high token-gen bursts).
- Engineering is scheduling a patch to make the fallback asynchronous and stream-safe (INF-9123). Marissa has submitted the change and we’ll backport it to trial clusters next week.

Next steps and asks:
1) Can Nebula re-run the demo Monday 26 Mar between 11:00–12:00 PT so we can join live and monitor packet-level traces?
2) We’ll provide a temporary SLA note for the pilot explaining the mitigation measures and expected window to fully remediate.
3) I’ll schedule an exec sync if you want a 15-min briefing on the technical plan.

We appreciate your patience — we’ll keep this prioritized until the patch is in.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
